topic: How your desire for 'the one' sabotages actual relationship quality
subject: relationships

sources.title: Intimate Relationships and Attitudes Toward Celebrities
Close relationship belief and self-change as predictors of romantic relationship quality in university students
Beyond Romantic Ideals: Marriage as a Dyadic Fortress for Containing Distress and Building Resilience

facts.claim: The belief that partners must meet all needs of each other is linked to the conflict subscale of relationship quality.
facts.quote: “We must meet all needs of each other” significantly predicted the conflict subscale

facts.claim: Romantic idealism is linked to the depth subscale of relationship quality.
facts.quote: “We must be able to change each other,” and “Romantic idealism” significantly predicted the depth subscale.

facts.claim: The belief that partners must meet all needs of each other is linked to the social support subscale of relationship quality.
facts.quote: “We must be completely open and honest with each other,” “We must do everything together,” “We must meet all needs of each other,” and “Romantic idealism” significantly predicted the social support subscale of relationship quality

facts.claim: Couples who engage in mutual emotional support have significantly lower levels of psychological distress than those with low dyadic engagement.
facts.quote: Furthermore, couples who engaged in mutual emotional support demonstrated significantly lower levels of psychological distress compared to those with low dyadic engagement.

facts.claim: Joint problemsolving is a significant predictor of resilience with a beta of 0.39 and a standard error of 0.07.
facts.quote: joint problemsolving (β = 0. 39, SE = 0. 07, p < . 001) were significant predictors of resilience

research.angle: While romantic idealism is linked to relationship depth and social support, the belief that partners must meet all needs of each other is linked to higher conflict.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that romantic idealism and mutual emotional support are associated with positive relationship qualities, but specific idealistic beliefs about meeting all needs are linked to conflict.
research.caveat: The studies provided are observational and do not establish a causal link between these beliefs and relationship outcomes.
